source: Williamson, Ji, Dwyer (2025) Syntactic Blind Spots: How Misalignment Leads to LLMs' Mathematical Errors
finding: Models fail more on questions whose syntax is complex. The authors read this as surface form cueing the wrong stored schema, and cite Chi et al. 1981 for the human version.
numbers: 5 open 7-8B models (Gemma, Granite, LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen), zero-shot, on GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith, ASDiv. Mean dependency-locality (DLT) score is higher on wrong answers on GSM8K for all 5 models (e.g. Qwen 29.01 vs 23.86, +5.15; Welch p<0.01). MultiArith: only 2 of 5 models positive.
limits: Correlational. Weak on short uniform datasets (MultiArith). Small 7-8B models only. DLT is a syntax proxy, not a measure of schema.
agent_relevance: Surface form can mis-trigger a solution template. An S0 gate should restate the problem in plain form before choosing a method.

source: Williamson, Ji, Dwyer (2025) Syntactic Blind Spots: How Misalignment Leads to LLMs' Mathematical Errors
finding: Rephrasing a failed question with the syntax of a question the model got right recovers many answers. A cheap restate-then-solve step.
numbers: Accuracy after rephrasing: GSM8K Gemma-7B 37.76 -> 46.02 (+8.26); Mistral-7B +11.68 (154 recovered); SVAMP Mistral +11.86; MultiArith Granite up to +15.5 pts; recovered counts range 2 (Qwen, MultiArith) to 210 (Gemma, ASDiv). The strongest model (Qwen) gains only 0.5-7.8 pts.
limits: Rephrasing was applied only to items already failed, so the gain is an upper bound (selection on failure, regression to the mean, no random-rephrase control).
agent_relevance: Supports a restate operator, but G2/G3/G7 apply: count it only against a random-rephrase control at equal tokens.

source: Han et al. (2024) Beyond Surface Structure: A Causal Assessment of LLMs' Comprehension Ability
finding: Direct test of deep versus surface structure in LLMs by causal mediation. Most models depend on deep structure, and the dependence grows with accuracy.
numbers: 12 models (Llama-2/3, Mistral/Mixtral, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, Claude-3/3.5 Sonnet) on 5 tasks incl. GSM8K and 2-digit multiplication. ADCE (deep-structure effect) is positive for most models; a random-weight Llama-3-70b gives 0. Linear fit of accuracy vs ADCE has R2>0.7.
limits: Deep structure is changed by masking or rephrasing key words, not by a physics-style sorting task.
agent_relevance: Counterweight to the pure pattern-matching story: stronger models do respond when the deep structure changes.

source: Han et al. (2024) Beyond Surface Structure: A Causal Assessment of LLMs' Comprehension Ability
finding: Closed models lean on deep structure; open models are more surface-sensitive, and surface sensitivity falls as model size grows.
numbers: Closed (GPT, Claude): deep-structure effect larger than surface effect. Open (Llama): more surface-sensitive, decreasing with scale (Llama-2 7b to 70b, Llama-3 8b to 70b).
quote: closed-source LLMs (e.g., GPT) rely more on deep structure, while open-source LLMs (e.g., Llama) are more surface-sensitive
limits: Group comparison across families; training data not controlled.
agent_relevance: The expert-novice gap in LLMs looks like a scale axis. A small base model may need forced deep-structure restatement; a large one less so.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: An Exploration in Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: Closest machine analogue to Chi et al. sorting. A strong LLM labels math questions by skill, clusters the labels, and at test time names the skill and gets exemplars of that skill. A schema index.
numbers: MATH: about 5000 fine-grained skills reduced to 117 coarse skills. GPT-4-0613 CoT 42.2 -> skill-based 53.88 (+11.6 over CoT; +3.5 over Complex CoT 50.30; +3.5 over topic-based 50.31).
limits: Skills named by a model, never checked against human expert sorting. The 42.2 CoT row is a fixed-exemplar prompt; the gain over a matched retrieval baseline is smaller.
agent_relevance: Routing by named skill beat routing by coarse topic (algebra, geometry). Candidate design for the memory index and S0 gate.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: An Exploration in Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: Skill-matched exemplars beat random exemplars, so the gain comes from matching, not from extra text. Skill labels from a strong model also help weaker models.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-4-0613: CoT 93.00, CoT+Random 92.87, CoT+Skill 94.31, +maj@5 95.38. GPT-3.5-Turbo: Retrieval-RSD 76.8 vs Skill 82.03. MATH program-aided: +7.52 over PAL.
limits: Ceiling on GSM8K (93% base). Single-run tables; no confidence intervals seen in the text read.
agent_relevance: Matching on the skill label is the useful part. Keep a random-exemplar control (G7).

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Adding one irrelevant sentence to a math problem breaks models. A novice-like surface reader uses the number from the irrelevant sentence.
numbers: GSM-IC (from GSM8K): of base problems solved by greedy baseline, no more than 18% were solved for all types of irrelevant information. Macro accuracy under 30% for most prompts; text-davinci-003 macro accuracy 0 on problems with more than 2 steps and role-overlap distractors.
limits: Old models (code-davinci-002, text-davinci-003, PaLM-era). Distractors made from templates.
agent_relevance: Relevance filtering is a schema skill. An S0 step should list the givens and mark which ones the solution needs.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Mitigations: exemplars that contain distractors, an explicit ignore instruction, and self-consistency each help; none close the gap.
numbers: Self-consistency (20 samples) adds over 11 pts micro accuracy, +35.5 pts for 0-shot CoT; the correct answer is in the 20 samples for 99.7% of problems; best macro accuracy of any method only 45%. The instruction 'feel free to ignore irrelevant information' raises COT, LTM and PROGRAM.
limits: Macro accuracy needs all variants right, a harsh measure.
agent_relevance: Voting finds the right answer in the pool but does not pick it (G4): recall 99.7% vs best macro 45%.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Same problem template with different names and numbers gives wide accuracy spread. Changing only names costs little; changing numbers costs more. A surface-versus-structure test built from templates.
numbers: 50 datasets per model; Gemma2-9B best-to-worst gap above 12%. Clause count lowers accuracy and raises variance; one model's mean across GSM-Symbolic / P1 / P2 is 91.7 -> 81.1 -> 72.4.
limits: The pattern-matching reading is an interpretation; contamination is a rival explanation. Newer reasoning models may do better (not checked here).
agent_relevance: Evaluate a scaffold on templated variants, not one fixed set, or gains are noise.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Plausible but irrelevant clauses (GSM-NoOp) cause large drops, and 8 shots of the same question do not fix it. Models map 'discount' to 'multiply' without reading the context.
numbers: Drop on GSM-NoOp up to over 65% (Phi-3-mini); o1-preview -17.5, Gemma-7b-it -20.6, Mistral-7b -24.0 pts. With 8 GSM-Symbolic shots of the same question, performance stayed within the standard deviation of the unaided NoOp result.
limits: Some later reports show smaller drops for newer models; not verified here.
agent_relevance: The model matches keywords to operations like a novice. Worked examples alone do not teach the filter; a code-checked given/needed split might.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models
finding: An agent loop that uses schema ideas: a problem distiller extracts key elements, retrieves a stored high-level thought template, instantiates it, and a buffer manager adds new templates after each solved task.
numbers: Table 1 with GPT-4: Game of 24 82.4 (CoT 11.0, ToT 74.0, Meta Prompting 67.0); MGSM 89.2; Geometric Shapes 93.6 (Meta 78.2); Checkmate-in-One 86.4 (Meta 57.2); Python Puzzles 52.4; Date Understanding 88.2. About 12% of the cost of multi-query methods.
limits: Authors' own runs; no independent replication read. Ablations without distiller or meta-buffer lower accuracy (shown in a figure; exact values not extracted).
agent_relevance: A concrete design for memory plus S0: distil, retrieve template, instantiate. Test against a no-buffer arm at equal tokens.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models
finding: Template reuse depends on the buffer manager: accuracy rises round by round with it and does not without it.
numbers: Round-by-round curves in the paper: upward trend with buffer manager, flat without. Six template categories.
limits: Tasks with repeated structure (Game of 24, Checkmate). Little evidence on structurally novel problems.
agent_relevance: Memory helps when new problems share deep structure with stored ones; add a miss path for novel ones.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover: Large Language Models Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
finding: The model selects atomic reasoning modules, adapts them, and composes one task-level structure, then reuses it for every instance of the task.
numbers: PaLM 2-L: BBH 56 direct, 60 CoT, 67 Self-Discover; T4D 30 / 40 / 69; MATH 45 / 42 / 50.5. GPT-4 direct: BBH 58, MATH 70.5. Beats CoT-self-consistency by over 20% with 10-40x less inference compute. Of MATH failures, 74.7% were computation errors, not structure.
limits: MATH uses a 200-item subsample; the gain on MATH is small.
agent_relevance: A task-level schema is cheap (once per task type). Structure is not the main bottleneck on MATH; arithmetic checks matter more.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in Large Language Models
finding: Ask the model to first state the principle or concept behind a question, then solve with it. The machine form of expert sorting by principle.
numbers: MMLU Physics / Chemistry: PaLM-2L base 66.4 / 70.9, CoT 65 / 75.3, Step-Back 73.2 / 81.8. GPT-4 base 69.4 / 80.9, CoT 82.9 / 85.3, Step-Back 84.5 / 85.6. Llama2-70B base 51.9 / 55.7, Step-Back 64.8 / 66.7.
limits: On GPT-4 Step-Back beats CoT by only 1.6 and 0.3 pts, within the stated spread.
agent_relevance: Principle-first helps weaker models most. It is not a free win on strong ones.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in Large Language Models
finding: Error analysis shows that recalling the principle is not the bottleneck. After step-back, most remaining errors are in reasoning and maths.
numbers: On MMLU high-school Physics, Step-Back corrected 20.5% of baseline errors and introduced 11.9% new ones. More than 90% of its errors are not Principle errors; Reasoning and Math errors dominate.
limits: Authors annotated a sample.
agent_relevance: Naming the right schema is necessary but far from sufficient. Pair S0 with checks (G3).

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
finding: The model writes its own related problems with solutions, then solves the target. Analogical prompting, from Polya's 'do you know a related problem'.
numbers: GSM8K / MATH, GPT-3.5-turbo: 5-shot CoT 76.7 / 34.9 vs self-generated exemplars 77.8 / 37.3. text-davinci-003 GSM8K 14.8 (0-shot) -> 61.0. PaLM2 MATH 27.1 -> 34.8.
limits: Needs a large model: with text-curie-001 and text-davinci-001 retrieved few-shot CoT is better. GSM8K gain small for GPT-3.5.
agent_relevance: Self-recall of related problems replaces a memory store only above a size threshold; with a small base model use stored examples.

source: Li et al. (2024) GSM-Plus: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating the Robustness of LLMs as Mathematical Problem Solvers
finding: Eight perturbations of GSM8K show robustness far below benchmark accuracy. Distractor insertion and added operations hurt CoT and LtM most.
numbers: 10,552 question variations; 25 LLMs; 4 prompts. GPT-4 performance drop rate (PDR) 8.23%; CodeLlama 7B / 13B / 34B PDR 40.56 / 39.71 / 34.27%. Prompt test on 120 seed questions and 960 variations: no prompt (CoT, PoT, LtM, complexity-CoT) matched seed-level accuracy on all variations.
limits: Variations written with GPT-4; humans revised 18.85%.
agent_relevance: Test the scaffold on perturbed variants as well as originals.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with Large Language Models
finding: Reordering the facts of a problem, with the same content, changes accuracy a lot. Models do best when the order of the givens matches the order of the solution steps.
numbers: Deductive tasks: drop over 30% when premises are shuffled; GPT-3.5 and Gemini 1.0 Pro fall from over 65% to below 25% in some orders. R-GSM: 220 original/reordered GSM8K pairs with the same answer; accuracy significantly lower after reordering.
limits: Logic tasks are synthetic. Effect smaller in stronger models.
agent_relevance: Experts rebuild the problem in solution order. A restate operator that sorts givens by use is testable.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) When 'A Helpful Assistant' Is Not Really Helpful: Personas in System Prompts Do Not Improve Performances of LLMs
finding: Telling a model it is an expert does not make it answer like one. Personas do not raise accuracy on factual questions.
numbers: 162 roles (6 relationship types, 8 expertise domains), 4 model families, 2,410 MMLU questions. Most personas show no significant effect vs no persona; picking the best persona per question is near random.
limits: Factual QA, not multi-step maths.
agent_relevance: Do not use an expert persona as the schema. Expertise must come from structure (G4).

source: Xu et al. (2023) ExpertPrompting: Instructing Large Language Models to be Distinguished Experts
finding: Detailed, auto-written expert identities improve answers on instruction data when a model judges them.
numbers: GPT-4 judge prefers expert-identity answers 48.5% vs 23% for vanilla answers (rest ties); 500 prompts.
limits: Judge is a model (favours longer text, G5). No ground-truth accuracy. Conflicts in kind with the persona-accuracy result above.
agent_relevance: Persona gains appear in model-judged style, not measured accuracy; treat with G5 caution.

source: Yang et al. (2025) ReasonFlux: Hierarchical LLM Reasoning via Scaling Thought Templates
finding: A library of about 500 thought templates is retrieved per problem, and a model is trained to plan a template sequence. A trained form of schema retrieval.
numbers: MATH-500 91.2% (6.7 pts above o1-preview); AIME 2024 56.7% with a 32B model (27 pts above o1-preview, 45 above DeepSeek-V3); OlympiadBench 63.3%.
limits: Training plus inference system, so gain is not from templates alone. Self-reported.
agent_relevance: Template libraries can reach about 500 entries and help hard maths, but need training; our scaffold has none.

source: Yu, He, Ying (2024) Thought Propagation: An Analogical Approach to Complex Reasoning with LLMs
finding: The model proposes analogous problems, solves them, and reuses the results to correct its first answer.
numbers: From the abstract: about +12% absolute for optimal Shortest-path Reasoning, +13% human preference in Creative Writing, +15% task completion in LLM-Agent planning.
limits: Graph and writing tasks, not maths. Read abstract and intro only.
agent_relevance: Analogy search needs a solved-problem store, and wrong analogies can carry errors across.

source: Search finding 2026-11: no LLM replication of the Chi et al. sorting task found
finding: One completed search found no study in which an LLM sorts physics or maths problems and its groups are compared with expert and novice sorts. Later search quota ran out, so this gap is not confirmed.
numbers: 0 studies found in 1 completed search.
limits: Absence of evidence under tool limits.
agent_relevance: Open question and possible own experiment: have the model sort 20 problems against a labelled deep-structure key.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover: Large Language Models Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
finding: Structures found by one model transfer to other models, so a schema can be built once by a strong model and reused by a weak one.
numbers: Abstract: structures found with PaLM 2-L work with GPT-4, and GPT-4 structures work with Llama2. Self-Discover beats direct answering on 23 of 25 BBH tasks and CoT on 21 of 25 (PaLM 2-L, zero-shot).
limits: Transfer shown on the authors' tasks; per-model numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Same direction as the skill-label result: schemas made by a strong model can be stored and used by a cheaper one.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) When 'A Helpful Assistant' Is Not Really Helpful
finding: Matching the persona's field to the question's field helps only a little.
numbers: Mixed-effects model: in-domain persona coefficient 0.004 (p<0.01), i.e. about 0.4 points of accuracy.
limits: Effect is statistically detectable but tiny; factual MMLU questions only.
agent_relevance: Even a domain-matched expert label is nearly worthless for accuracy; routing must come from problem structure, not a role name.
